name: National Museum of the US Air Force
unique: The largest military aviation museum in the world: B-17s, a B-2 stealth bomber, an SR-71 and the actual Memphis Belle, all free.
buzz: People plan two hours and stay five; the hangars are enormous and the volunteer veterans are a highlight. Free parking, too.

name: Cedar Point
unique: The roller coaster capital of the world on a Lake Erie peninsula: 18 coasters, including dragster style launches and a wooden hybrid that regularly tops global rankings.
buzz: Coaster fans plan entire trips around it; everyone warns about fast lane pricing and closing time traffic. Go midweek in early June.

name: Cleveland Museum of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Asian art, medieval armor, Impressionism and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and world class, with a beautiful building and a good cafe. One of the best museums in the country.

name: Hocking Hills
unique: Recess Cave, Old Man's Cave and Cedar Falls: a sandstone gorge system of waterfalls, hemlock forest and huge overhangs you can walk behind.
buzz: The trails are crowded on summer weekends and magical in winter; the Grandma Gatewood trail links the main falls. Book a cabin early.

name: Ohio State Reformatory
customer: Film fans, ghost hunters, history buffs
unique: A towering Romanesque prison used in The Shawshank Redemption, with cell blocks six tiers high, solitary confinement and overnight paranormal investigations.
buzz: The architecture is stunning and the Shawshank connection brings film people; the ghost tours are a separate, spookier ticket.

name: Cincinnati Museum Center
unique: Three museums in the Art Deco Union Terminal: natural history, Cincinnati history and a children's museum.
buzz: The building is worth the trip alone, and the history museum has a great model of the city.

name: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium
unique: A zoo and aquarium with polar bears, manatees, a water park and a golf course, on the Scioto River.
buzz: The manatee rescue and the polar bears are the highlights, and the water park makes it a full day.

name: Otherworld
unique: A 32,000 square foot immersive art installation of more than forty rooms, half escape game and half dreamscape, where you open drawers and follow a loose story through the space.
buzz: The scale is impressive and the details reward curiosity; it is less narrative than Meow Wolf and more playground. Good for teens.
customer: Young adults, friends, families with teens

name: Serpent Mound
unique: A quarter mile effigy of a serpent built by indigenous people two thousand years ago on a crater rim, aligned to the solstice, with no consensus on what it meant.
buzz: People describe a strange calm on the ridge; the museum is small and the site is best at sunrise or dusk.

name: American Sign Museum
unique: Two warehouses of neon, bulb and painted signs from the last century, with a Main Street of storefronts and a workshop where restorers bring dead signs back to light.
buzz: The neon room is a photographer's dream and the history of sign making is unexpectedly interesting; allow ninety minutes.

name: Cincinnati Zoo
unique: The second oldest zoo in the country, with hippos, gorillas, a train and the Fiona the hippo story.
buzz: Well laid out and shady, with the hippo exhibit as the draw. Allow half a day.

name: Franklin Park Conservatory
unique: A glasshouse with biomes from rainforest to desert, plus a butterfly garden and a collection of Chihuly glass.
buzz: The Chihuly glass among the plants is the draw, and the butterfly house is a kid favorite.

name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
company: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
unique: I.M. Pei's glass pyramid on the lake, holding Prince's guitar, Janis Joplin's Porsche and a hall of signatures that reads like a century of American noise.
buzz: The films and artifacts are stronger than the interactives; allow four hours. The lakefront setting is best at sunset.

name: Toledo Museum of Art
unique: A free art museum with a strong glass collection, Old Masters and a sculpture garden, in a Greek Revival building.
buzz: The glass collection is the local specialty and the museum is free. A surprise for a mid sized city.

name: Kings Island
unique: The Beast, still the longest wooden coaster in the world, plus a kids' area and a water park in a wooded park north of Cincinnati.
buzz: The Beast at night is a genuine rite of passage; lines are manageable midweek. Food is standard park fare.

name: West Side Market
unique: A 1912 market hall with a vaulted ceiling, butcher stalls, pierogi stands and produce vendors under one roof.
buzz: The building is beautiful and the food is cheap. Go hungry and bring cash.

name: Amish Country
unique: The largest Amish settlement in the world: draft horses on the road, bulk food stores, furniture workshops and a bakery culture that runs on lard and butter.
buzz: Go on a weekday, respect the no photos signs, and eat at a family style restaurant. The flea market is enormous on Thursdays.

name: Great Lakes Science Center
unique: A science center on the lake with a NASA Glenn visitor center, a domed theater and hands on exhibits.
buzz: The NASA exhibits are the draw and the lakefront location is nice. Good for kids.

name: Put-in-Bay
unique: A Lake Erie island reached by ferry, with golf carts, a 352-foot monument to a War of 1812 naval victory and a bar scene that gets loud by 3pm.
buzz: Rent a golf cart and circumnavigate the island; the wineries and the monument are the calm counterpoint. Ferries sell out on summer weekends.

name: Loveland Castle
unique: A medieval style castle built by hand from river stones by a scoutmaster and his troop, with a dungeon, a great hall and a sword in a stone.
buzz: It is homemade and earnest and kids love it; the story of the builder is the best part. Cheap and quick.
